source.extraction_method: Manual extraction from current TypeScript behavior; every rule below is labelled implementation-derived and cites the implementation lines used.
source.determinism: Do not include timestamps. Update only when current TypeScript behavior or measured feedback-loop metrics change.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Default layout uses a 120 px semantic column pitch, a 10 px diagram-js-compatible center grid, spine Y=70, lower tracks at Y=180 and Y=430, 140 px track gap, and nominal channels at Y=140/280/560 before dynamic channel planning.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Events are 36x36, gateways 50x50, and all other non-subprocess node types default to 100x80. Expanded subprocess container dimensions are computed dynamically from a recursive child layout: the children's bounding box plus SUBPROCESS_PAD_H=40px on each side and SUBPROCESS_PAD_V=30px on each side, with minimums of 360x200.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Sequence flows whose source or target belongs to a different immediate process/subprocess container are rejected before layout; existing BPMN diagrams are then removed and regenerated.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: A DFS marks back-edges as loop-backs. The primary spine starts at the first start event and follows non-back-edge outgoing flows, scoring end events high, subprocesses and reject/error/fail/give-up branches low, and looping targets lower than completion exits. During branch-track assignment, named exception branches normally use the upper track, except terminal exception branches targeting an end event, which use the lower track so a gateway can fan out horizontally and downward.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Spine nodes occupy increasing columns with a 50 px edge clearance derived from actual node widths. When lane membership is declared, top-level lane members prefer deterministic tracks based on lane order; otherwise branches are placed breadth-first relative to their parent. Exception branches go upward, ordinary non-spine branches go downward unless a loop-back spans the gateway, same-track nodes are shifted fractionally to avoid width-based overlap without introducing a whole-column gap, and direct same-track terminal flows are repaired to the same clearance after packing. buildTrackColMapsWithDim accepts effective dimensions so recursively sized subprocesses drive column/track spacing.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Sequential flow-node paths use a uniform 50 px edge-to-edge clearance, matching the default horizontal spacing used by bpmn-js for newly placed flow nodes. Node widths contribute half-widths on both sides of each gap.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: When an upper track exists, it becomes the visual spine; lower tracks are offset from the default 140 px track pitch. Tracks containing nodes taller than 80 px add cumulative vertical clearance.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Expanded subprocesses are laid out recursively. computeProcessLayout is called on the subprocess flowElements in local coordinates; the resulting bounding box plus SUBPROCESS_PAD_H=40 px left/right and SUBPROCESS_PAD_V=30 px top/bottom determines the container size (minimum 360x200). After the outer layout finalizes parent positions, layoutSubProcessChildrenRecursive translates child node layouts to absolute coordinates in the parent layoutNodes map with isSubProcessChild=true, preserving grid-sized translations and centered content when the minimum container is larger than the child bounds.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Boundary events are positioned on their attached host's top or bottom boundary. Multiple boundary events on one host alternate sides deterministically. Outgoing branch target activities without competing incoming flows are shifted to the upper track; traversal continues from each shifted target so its downstream nodes, including terminal end events, inherit the branch track and remain near the branch. The leftmost exception target may align to the primary outgoing target column while later branch targets retain their columns. Routes first leave through the attached side before using an orthogonal channel and enter upper-track targets through their top boundary, preventing sequence flows from crossing the host body.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Boundary-event labels prefer the side away from their attached host, trying centered and deterministic lateral offsets before falling back to normal event-label placement. This keeps labels from being printed inside the host activity while preserving collision-aware selection.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: When a bpmn:Collaboration exists, processes referenced by participants are excluded from standalone per-process BPMNDiagram generation. createCollaborationDi emits a single BPMNDiagram containing: participant pool shapes with isHorizontal=true sized from content bounding box plus PAD_LEFT=60, PAD_RIGHT=30, PAD_TOP=30, PAD_BOTTOM=30 (participants stacked with 40 px gaps); lane shapes with isHorizontal=true; all flow-node shapes and sequence-flow edges from each participant process (shifted to absolute coordinates via dx/dy); and named message-flow edges. Message flows are routed through the same repairSegmentCollisions pipeline sequence flows use: a candidate 4-point mid-line route is repaired against a collaboration-wide obstacle set (every participant's flow nodes, merged container boundary strips, and every already-placed sequence- and message-flow route), then validated, falling back to the unrepaired candidate if repair does not validate. Standalone processes (not in any collaboration) receive per-process BPMNDiagram with lane shapes derived from member node bounds.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Disconnected top-level components are packed after local layout, preferring a compact row below the main start-event component when their total width is at most 75% of the main component, otherwise using the landscape A4 aspect-ratio score. Node center X values are first snapped to the 75 + n*120 semantic grid when the move is at most 2 px, then all node centers are quantized to the configured 10 px compatibility grid.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Final node centers are quantized independently on X and Y using gridSize, defaulting to 10 px to match diagram-js grid snapping. Intermediate orthogonal route points are quantized when the resulting polyline remains orthogonal; shape-boundary attachment points remain determined by node geometry.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Loop-back and bypass channels are derived from the occupied node band with 30 px clearance. Channel planning is container-scoped (planContainerScopedChannels): nodes are grouped by their immediate container -- the top-level diagram, or one expanded subprocess's own children -- and each group's band and lane assignment is computed independently, so a subprocess-internal channel is bounded by that subprocess's own content, never by the outer diagram's. Overlapping channel spans within a container are assigned separate 30 px lanes using a two-pass greedy plan before final waypoints are emitted. Same-track gateway bypasses with an upper-track branch use an upper channel so they do not cross that branch; other same-track bypasses use the lower channel.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Visibility-route candidates are filtered for orthogonality and minimum-turn constraints, then selected deterministically by the configured turn preference, path length, and serialized-point tie-breaker. The default policy requires orthogonal routes, permits zero minimum turns, prefers fewer turns, and imposes no additional path-length factor.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Waypoint routing handles boundary-event departures, gateway-to-gateway upside bypasses, loop-backs, same-track forward flows, gateway branches up/down, same-track gateway bypasses through dedicated channels, downward exception routes around intervening content, upper-track exits to end events, merges into gateways, and a final orthogonal fallback. These same cases route subprocess-internal (child-to-child) flows too, not a separate stub -- obstacle scans that exclude subprocess children (the short-circuit direct check, the same-track forward-flow check, and the downward gateway-branch check) are container-scoped via inSameContainer, so an internal flow is only obstructed by its own container's siblings and an external flow is unaffected.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Crowded node-side attach points are fanned out deterministically by flow id. Routed polylines are repaired by enforcing outward departure, treating nearby nodes, protected central portions of every existing path, and pool/lane container boundary obstacles as obstacles, trying visibility routes and ordered 15 px nudges up to 300 px, and side-approaching blocked final legs. External routes treat expanded subprocesses as opaque obstacles, while internal subprocess flows route against sibling content. Container boundary obstacles are thin strips -- pool top/bottom/right borders, the pool name-label gutter (solid), and lane dividers -- computed from lane/participant band geometry once known and passed into repairSegmentCollisions as `layout.containerObstacles`; the lane/pool interior itself is not an obstacle. Before serialization, every sequence flow must attach to both node boundaries, depart and arrive orthogonally outward, and use a source and target side compatible with clearly dominant horizontal or vertical separation; invalid restoration or fallback routes are rejected. Only validated gateway channel routes may be reasserted after this pass; non-gateway routes are never overwritten after validation.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Both the channel-span-recording pass and the post-repair edge-vs-edge avoidance pass iterate flows in orderFlowsForRouting's order -- ascending structural span (column + track distance between endpoints), then source id, then target id -- instead of source-document order, so inserting an unrelated sequence flow earlier in the XML cannot renumber or re-route flows that were already fine. The post-repair pass also skips re-running repair on a route that already has zero obstacle hits (countRouteHits) and passes validateConnectionPoints, so a route is never perturbed by an obstacle set that changed after it was already correct.

rules.label: quality-gate
rules.rule: The feedback report records the exact edge pairs, edge/shape pairs, edge/subprocess-container pairs, and invalid endpoint attachments responsible for geometry defects. It also records invalid label bounds. The quality gate fails on any such defect while preserving details in metrics.json and command output so routing regressions can be traced to named BPMN elements.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Named events and gateways receive external BPMNLabel bounds. Candidate label positions vary by flow attachment directions, gateway shape, preferred top/bottom side, text width, and line count; single-line primary gateway labels align their top edge with a 4 px gap, while multi-line primary labels shift upward so their bottom edge aligns with the single-line label row. Snug candidates keep a 6 px horizontal clearance. When a selected gateway candidate needs multiple lines to avoid path or element collisions, the formatted line break is serialized into the element name so renderers display the intended rows. Candidates that collide with lanes, elements, or previously placed labels are rejected before fallback.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: The label solver uses an 8 px primary/alternate vertical gap for named events and a 6 px primary/alternate vertical gap for gateways; collision-free candidate selection can choose a different side or offset. This is a generalized parameterized heuristic, but the desired gateway-above versus gateway-below preference is not yet a complete formal rule.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Named sequence flows receive labels on a preferred horizontal segment of at least 30 px, or otherwise a vertical segment of at least 20 px. Horizontal labels are centered on the segment midpoint with a 2 px above-segment clearance when that side is selected. Edge labels are placed before node labels so node-label placement can avoid them.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: ensureLabelDi materializes default BPMNLabel rectangles for named events, gateways, and lanes when shape DI exists but label bounds do not; event/gateway defaults are 90x20 below the shape, and lane defaults are a 30 px tall rectangle rotated into the lane boundary.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: labelLayout reports missing label DI for named events/gateways/lanes, invalid label bounds, lane labels outside lane bounds, labels overlapping elements or labels, and labels outside containing lanes or participants.

metrics.definition: Counts BPMN XML elements by local name plus sequence flows, message flows, lanes, and data references for fixture coverage and regression slicing.
Computes diagram extents from shape bounds and edge waypoints as x, y, width, and height.
Counts non-container shape overlaps, total shape overlap area, and label-label overlaps from BPMN DI bounds.

Counts edge crossings, edge intersections with non-endpoint non-container shapes, route intersections with expanded subprocess, lane, and participant containers that neither endpoint belongs to, invalid source/target boundary attachments, total bends, Manhattan length, and non-orthogonal segments.

Checks every orthogonal edge segment against the 50 px default route unit, reporting non-multiple segments and the largest distance from a 50 px multiple. A route may contain multiple-unit segments and turns.

Measures edge-to-edge gaps for same-track, left-to-right sequence-flow endpoints with no intervening non-container shape, reporting count, minimum, maximum, and average gap in pixels. Longer bypass and loop flows are excluded.
Measures non-container shape center-X deviation from the implementation grid 75 + n*120, reported as average and maximum absolute deviation.
Compares named events, gateways, lanes, sequence/message flows, and data references against BPMN DI labels, reporting covered and missing label targets.

Records invalid label bounds plus label intersections with non-own shapes and non-own routes. Container bounds that contain a label are treated as valid containment rather than a collision. These diagnostics guide label-solver work and remain informational until the persisted fixture baseline is collision-free.

Reports count, minimum, maximum, and average vertical gap between named event/gateway shapes and their BPMNLabel bounds, grouped by element class. Use this to compare gateway labels with the 8 px event-label baseline.

feedback_observations.observation: The overall three-row grid, happy-path spine, branch spacing, event-subprocess alignment, and label-to-node distances are good. The exclusive gateway label 'Order valid?' could use a slightly larger below-node gap; the above-node labels 'Check in parallel' and 'Checks complete' could use a small consistent gap comparable to event labels.
feedback_observations.next_step: Continue visual review with another single label-placement target if needed.

loop: Run the report command to capture original/transformed images and deterministic metrics.
Collect feedback JSON with checkbox choices, Likert ratings, and comments.
Map low ratings and selected choices to this ruleset and the report metrics.
Change TypeScript behavior, update this artifact from the changed implementation, and rerun targeted reports.
